text:
Samira (Support): FYI - high-priority customer (Acme) hitting intermittent 504s / timeouts on the hosted text-generation endpoint since 09:12 UTC. They see spikes during bursts, roughly 30-90s after increased traffic. They opened a support ticket and asked for root cause.
Alex (oncall-sre): Looking now. Can you paste a sample request id or trace?
Samira (Support): Ticket includes request id req_0a7f... and a gateway trace: gateway->router 504, backend returned 502/timeout. No auth errors. They shared a curl repro hitting /v1/generate with stream=false.
Samira (Support): sample log from gateway: `"upstream_response_time": "31.412", "status": 504, "upstream_status": 502`
Alex (oncall-sre): I see a cluster-wide scale event around the times. deploy-bot posted KEDA scaledown/scaleup events.
deploy-bot: ScalerEvent: ScaledObject 'ro-modelpool-textgen-prod' scaled to 0 -> 2 (reason: activePrometheusRule threshold). Polling interval: 30s, cooldown: 300s.
Mike (Eng-Infra): Can you check pods readiness? If pods are coming up but readiness failing, gateway might route to not-ready pods or connection stuck.
Anna (Eng-Runtime): I pulled recent pod logs for one of the cold starts. Model init logs show long tensor/PT load steps. Key snippets:```
[2026-03-15T09:12:22Z] INFO model:init starting model load
[2026-03-15T09:12:46Z] WARN kvcache: warmup miss, initializing cache
[2026-03-15T09:13:11Z] INFO runtime: grpc server listening on 0.0.0.0:8081
[2026-03-15T09:13:40Z] ERROR probe: /health failed (503) - readiness=false
[2026-03-15T09:13:55Z] INFO model:init completed, kvcache primed
```
Anna (Eng-Runtime): Readiness probe is against /health which returns OK only after model init and cache priming. Probe timeout is 5s with initialDelaySeconds 10. For big models that can be 30-60s init.
Alex (oncall-sre): So KEDA starts pods, gateway starts routing after endpoints show ready but readiness only flips late -> some requests during init see 5xx/timeouts. Also KEDA polling interval 30s + scaleToZero leads to cold starts hitting customers.
Kevin (Platform): config check: ScaledObject has scaleTargetRef to Deployment 'ro-textgen-prod' and triggers on queue length and a prometheus rule. HPA is not attached. I also see minReplicaCount=0, cooldownPeriod=300.
Mike (Eng-Infra): Reproduction steps: I ran a quick load that spikes QPS from 1->40 (short burst). Observed 504s consistently within 20-45s window after spike. Curl loop I used:```
for i in {1..80}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' & done; wait;```
Mike (Eng-Infra): Logs during repro: some pods created but readiness failed until ~30-60s, gateway 504s peaked at t+25s.
Anna (Eng-Runtime): Root causes: 1) scale-to-zero pattern + long model init time 2) readiness probe only flips after cache priming causing router to mark endpoints ready late 3) KEDA poll interval/cooldown allows for larger gaps and bursts.
Samira (Support): Customer asked why the API doesn't queue or autoscale faster. Are there immediate mitigations?
Alex (oncall-sre): Short-term mitigations: - Increase minReplicaCount to 1 for hot customers or model pools - Reduce KEDA cooldown/polling interval (e.g., poll 5-10s) - Increase readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds? (No, that would delay readiness further) - Implement a lightweight readiness that returns ready earlier but add traffic shaping / warmup endpoint
Kevin (Platform): We should not flip readiness early since requests routed to a pod before model is ready will 5xx. Better approach: Keep readiness strict and have a warmup path that controller calls to fully initialize model before marking ready. Alternatively, set minReplicaCount=1 for production pools used by paying customers.
Anna (Eng-Runtime): We have a warmup RPC in runtime but controller/ScaledObject doesn't call it. We can add a preStart init container to pull weights and prime disk cache, and have a post-start hook that calls the warmup endpoint, then toggle readiness via a file-based probe. That requires infra changes.
Mike (Eng-Infra): Quick config change we can do now: bump minReplicaCount=1 for ro-modelpool-textgen-prod while we iterate. Also reduce KEDA cooldown to 60s and pollingInterval to 10s to make scale-up faster in bursts. Risk: cost increase.
Alex (oncall-sre): I'll patch the ScaledObject on prod in the safe change window and monitor 15m. Will also add a temporary routing rule to increase gateway retry/backoff for 5xx during scale events (2 retries with jitter).
Samira (Support): I've told Acme we'll apply a fix and keep them updated. They've agreed to a brief maintenance window.
Kevin (Platform): Action items: - Alex: apply minReplicaCount=1 + cooldown->60 + polling->10 on modelpool (done as patch ID: #PR-7423) - Anna: prepare runtime change for warmup hook & file-probe design doc (ETA 2d) - Mike: create rollback playbook and monitor dashboard (ETA 4h)
Alex (oncall-sre): Patch applied to staging, rolling to prod now. Repro test: same curl burst, staging shows no 504s after change (sustained 40 QPS -> pods stayed warm).
deploy-bot: Deployment ro-modelpool-textgen-prod scaled minReplicas 1/3 (requested).
Mike (Eng-Infra): Monitoring notes: added a temporary dashboard tile showing scale events, pod init durations, readiness flip time, and gateway 5xx rate. Threshold alert if gateway 5xx > 1% during scale windows.
Anna (Eng-Runtime): For the long-term: design doc will propose (a) warmup API callchain from controller (b) model-shared cache priming outside request path (c) config for per-model coldstart SLOs and minReplica defaults.
Samira (Support): Customer updated: after we applied the minReplica change and retries they saw traffic stabilized and no 504s during the test window. They flagged cost concerns but prefer reliability.
Alex (oncall-sre): Closing loop: root cause = scale-to-zero + model coldstart duration + KEDA polling/cooldown causing insufficient warm pod capacity for bursts. Fixes: short-term config changes (minReplicaCount=1, lower cooldown/polling, gateway retries) + long-term runtime/controller warmup flow.
Kevin (Platform): I'll open a follow-up ticket to standardize minReplica defaults for high-priority modelpools and add an internal runbook. Ticket: PLAT-2891.
Samira (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll send the customer post-mortem and schedule a sync with Acme for cost vs reliability tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
Alex (oncall-sre): Marking incident resolved for now. Will keep monitoring for 2h. :eyes:
